development: User-supplied renderer contract requires exactly three top-level keys, minified single-line JSON, obj/text elements, normalised y1-x1-y2-x2 bboxes, and strict background-versus-elements separation.
prompting_impact: When this renderer profile is requested, emit only aspect_ratio, high_level_description and compositional_deconstruction; use concrete one-subject obj elements, dedicated text elements, and no unsupported generic JSON fields.

development: Google's current documentation states that Imagen is deprecated and was shut down on 17 August 2026, with migration to Nano Banana recommended.
prompting_impact: Do not recommend Imagen for new work or treat its prompt guide as an active route; route current Google image generation to Nano Banana variants.

development: Black Forest Labs documents Klein consumer-hardware operation with as little as 13 GB VRAM in its launch information.
prompting_impact: Strengthen local model routing towards Klein on a 16 GB RTX 4070 Ti SUPER while retaining precision, offload, resolution and frontend caveats outside the prompt.

development: Google's image-generation documentation, updated 26 August 2026, now defines four distinct Nano Banana routes: Nano Banana 2 Lite (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image), Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image), Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro Image), and legacy Nano Banana (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image). Google recommends Nano Banana 2 as the general default, Lite for latency and cost, and Pro for the most complex professional work.
prompting_impact: Route ordinary generation and multi-reference editing to Nano Banana 2; use Pro for complex brand, localisation, grounding, or precision work; use Lite for fast low-cost single-pass work, not multi-reference or long multi-turn editing. Do not treat legacy Gemini 2.5 Flash Image as the default.

development: Gemini 3 image models accept up to 14 total references, but their supported reference roles differ. Gemini 3.1 Flash Image supports fidelity for up to 10 objects and resemblance for up to four characters; Gemini 3 Pro Image supports up to six objects, five characters, and three style references. Gemini 3.1 Flash Image uniquely supports video-to-image and Google Image Search grounding.
prompting_impact: Assign every input a clear object, character, style, scene, or video role and choose the model by reference type rather than total count alone. Route video-derived stills and image-search-grounded generation to Nano Banana 2; route multi-style professional composites to Pro.

development: OpenAI released gpt-image-2 on 21 April 2026 as its current image generation and editing model. OpenAI's deprecation schedule directs users of gpt-image-1, gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-image-1.5, and chatgpt-image-latest to gpt-image-2 before their 2026 shutdown dates.
prompting_impact: Use GPT Image 2 as the current API target for new generation and editing workflows. Preserve the existing structured prompting and iterative edit guidance, but do not recommend older GPT Image aliases for new builds.

development: GPT Image 2 automatically processes every image input at high fidelity, so the API does not accept a user-set input_fidelity value. It also accepts flexible output resolutions and supports transparent PNG or WebP backgrounds in preview.
prompting_impact: Do not advise setting input_fidelity for GPT Image 2. Continue to label references by role and state preservation constraints; use the API size and background controls for exact output requirements. For transparent edits, explicitly preserve transparency on every turn.

development: Krea's official open-weight prompting guide recommends natural-language prompts and states that long, detailed prompts yield the best results for Krea 2 Turbo, while minimal prompts can still work. Exact visible text should be placed in quotation marks. The open Turbo checkpoint is an eight-step text-to-image model with CFG disabled and supports up to 2K output.
prompting_impact: For open-weight Krea 2 Turbo, use a coherent detailed natural-language description when control matters and quote exact visible wording. Do not carry the hosted-interface shorthand rule over as a universal Krea 2 rule; keep hosted controls and open-weight prompting distinct.

development: A reproducible community ComfyUI guide reports Krea 2 Turbo FP8 generation on RTX 3060 12 GB and RTX 4080 16 GB systems, using a roughly 13 GB FP8 checkpoint. Krea publishes no official minimum-VRAM figure for the 12B/13B-class model.
prompting_impact: Treat Krea 2 Turbo FP8 as an experimental but credible 16 GB local text-to-image option. Keep FP8, offload, frontend, resolution, and speed guidance outside the prompt and do not present 16 GB viability as an official Krea claim.

development: Qwen's official repository identifies Qwen-Image-2512 as the current open-weight text-to-image checkpoint and Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 as the current open-weight editing checkpoint. The separately announced Qwen-Image-2.0 unifies generation and editing but has no official open-weight release in the cited repository.
prompting_impact: For local workflows, route text-to-image to Qwen-Image-2512 and editing or multi-image consistency work to Qwen-Image-Edit-2511. Do not imply that Qwen-Image-2.0 is locally downloadable. Continue to label multiple inputs by role and use localised chained corrections for difficult edits.

development: xAI announced on September 2, 2026 that grok-imagine-image-quality will retire on November 2, 2026 and redirect to grok-imagine-image-2.0 at quality low. The replacement supports explicit low, medium or auto quality, up to five source images for editing, and 21:9 and 5:2 aspect ratios; auto currently serves low for generation and medium for editing.
prompting_impact: Route new Grok Imagine generation and editing to grok-imagine-image-2.0. Pin quality when cost or fidelity must be predictable, assign deliberate roles to multi-image edit inputs, and set aspect ratio through the API control rather than prompt prose alone.
